How to use this page

  1. Filter by layer, listing or country, or search any name, ticker or phrase (try “HBM”, “backstop” or “Texas”).
  2. Solid chips are the company's home layers; dashed chips are other layer dossiers that discuss it at length. Every chip links to that layer's page.
  3. Every number carries its period and a provenance badge: R reported, G guidance, E third-party estimate, A Atlas estimate.
  4. The network at the bottom shows who pays whom among the 25 most connected companies, including the circular deals.

Tickers are primary listings. “Private · X” names the owner of an unlisted company or unit. Figures are the latest in the dossiers as of 25 Sep 2026; see each layer page for sources.

Who depends on whom

Twenty-five companies sit at the center of the build-out. Follow the arrows to see who pays whom: customers above, suppliers below, and investment flowing back up.

Solid blue arrows are purchases: the customer pays the supplier for cloud capacity, chips, wafers or tools. Dashed orange arrows are investments, warrants and guarantees: the investor puts money into the company at the arrowhead. Where a dashed arrow runs opposite a solid one, the supplier is funding its own customer, which is the circular financing described in W02 and W11. Line width shows the contract value where one is disclosed. Hover or tab to a company to isolate its relationships.

What the network shows

Two companies sit in the middle of almost every loop. NVIDIA is paid by every hyperscaler and neocloud, and it has put equity or guarantees into OpenAI, Anthropic, xAI, CoreWeave and Intel. OpenAI has committed about $710B of disclosed cloud contracts (Oracle $300B, Azure $250B, AWS $138B, CoreWeave $22.4B) while raising money from three of the same suppliers.
